candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

We were impressed with your test submission and would be delighted to bring you on board to update our Leadership Interview Questions You'll Most Likely Be Asked book!

To ensure we are aligned from the outset, we’d like to explain the project’s complete scope so you know exactly what the work will involve.

**Project Aim**

Our goal is to revise the first edition of the Leadership Interview Questions book so that it aligns with present-day industry standards and remains useful to current readers. The book is a quick-reference interview preparation guide for managers, team leads, and senior professionals who have 4 to 5+ years of experience, as well as people entering leadership positions for the first time. We also want to incorporate a global viewpoint by illustrating how interview questions and answers may differ across countries and industries.

**Project Stages**

**1. Reviewing and updating existing content (Milestone 1)**
We’ll provide the first edition for your review. While examining the 250 questions, we’d like your recommendations on which questions should be removed because they are outdated, no longer align with the modern leadership environment, or duplicate other questions in the book.

--Refining the full question set according to your review

--Writing answers for the content that remains. Please keep in mind that the answer layers previously discussed—interviewer’s intent, common mistakes, how to structure the answer, and answer framework—might not be suitable for every question. After we jointly finalize the question set, we can identify which questions require every layer and which only need a couple.

**2. Adding new chapters (Milestone 2)**
We would like to add several new sections/chapters and welcome your input on how best to shape them:

--A pre-interview preparation checklist. Because the intended readers already have professional experience, this section may benefit from focusing on leadership-specific preparation instead of basic advice. We’d like to include any tips that are particularly applicable to leadership-level interviews.

--Remote & Hybrid Leadership questions

--Questions candidates can ask the interviewer

--How to use AI for interview preparation (prompts, techniques, tools)

--Questions created specifically for first-time leaders

In your response to the previous briefing, you identified the chapters you considered most relevant, which was helpful. However, unless a chapter contains question & answer content, we expect all chapters to remain short. The AI chapter appears to offer readers the most distinctive benefit. Given the current environment, knowing how to apply AI to different tasks is important, so that chapter must be included.

**3. Hybrid Experience (Milestone 3)**

--Our books are intended to provide a hybrid learning experience because some readers prefer not to go through a book cover-to-cover. In addition to the book itself, we want to provide online companion materials such as checklists, AI prompts, body-language videos, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, and any other resources you might recommend.

**A Note on Word Count**

While reviewing the existing content and preparing additions, please monitor the book’s total word count. Our limit is 50K words, while the first edition contains approximately 37K, which initially leaves about 13K words available. However, because the revision will be extensive and some questions will be removed, we expect that additional space may become available. The completed book must not exceed 50K words overall.

We have also included our author guidelines for the Interview series. Please review them and tell us if any part requires further explanation. Link to author guidelines: [URL_002]

Here is also the complete book in Google Doc format. We’re working in Google Doc so changes can be tracked, although we can provide a PDF as a reference if that is more convenient: [URL_003]

After the project starts, we will provide the actual working manuscript and make the appropriate changes.

We’re looking forward to collaborating with you on this, [FREELANCER_NAME_001]. Please reach out if you have any questions. If a call would help address your concerns, we can arrange one.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

For Milestone 1:

- Yes, we agree that reducing the number of questions is appropriate. We would appreciate a brief explanation for every question you remove. Please use the Google Doc we provided: delete the relevant questions and leave a comment stating your rationale. (At this point, we cannot offer a downloadable version of the document. You have commenting access, which allows you to delete content in suggesting mode and include a comment explaining your reasoning.)

After the question list has been approved, we’ll prepare a working manuscript that contains only the selected questions, making it easier to develop those items directly.

- For the answer layers, our view is that each question should include at least two layers: how to frame the answer and a sample answer. The interviewer’s intent, common mistakes, and framework layers will not necessarily be relevant to every question.

- The deadline for this milestone will be incorporated into the schedule for the project as a whole.

For Milestone 2: New Chapters

- When we say "global perspective," we are not asking for separate chapters devoted to individual locations. Instead, it should be incorporated organically into the chapters already planned. For instance, a pre-interview checklist could explain how the process differs in the USA and India, or answer framing could vary between the US and the UK. A short introductory note would be suitable, explaining that the main audience is in the US and India while relevant tips throughout the book will point out differences from a global perspective.

Besides the US and India, we would also value your recommendations regarding other markets worth considering.

- There is no strict target, but we estimate that each chapter should generally be between 2.5k and 3.5k words. Depending on the subject and the detail it needs, a chapter may be shorter or a little longer. Since this is an interview questions book, theory-based chapters should ideally remain fairly concise.

For Milestone 3: Hybrid Companion Resources

- This stage is included in the complete project and should preferably be finished during the assigned project timeline. The milestones will not take place simultaneously, however; they will move forward sequentially, and each stage will start only after the prior one is finished. Accordingly, the third milestone will start when the manuscript is close to completion.

- Most hybrid-resource assets should ideally be delivered as finished products. For video concepts, however, you may submit scripts and we will take care of recording them. You will need to prepare the templates so our production team can build exactly what you envision.

We proposed those hybrid-resource examples because we believe they can distinguish this book in the market and allow readers to learn in visual and practical ways rather than through text alone. We would also welcome any ideas you have for companion materials that would work particularly well with this type of book.

General Queries

Regarding payment, the project’s total compensation is $300. Our plan is to divide it among three milestones at $100 each, with payment tied to completion of the deliverables agreed upon for each stage. If you prefer another milestone arrangement, though, we’re open to discussing it and finding a structure that suits both parties.

Contract: Yes, we will certainly provide one. The contract will be sent after all details have been settled and we are prepared to proceed.

We are targeting delivery of the final manuscript one month after the project begins, although that date is flexible. Since you now understand the project’s complete requirements and scope, please tell us what timeline would be manageable for you. The milestone structure we shared is our preferred approach, but you are welcome to propose a different breakdown, which we can discuss together.

Our editorial team will provide feedback during scheduled review periods throughout the process.

Please let us know if you have additional questions or would like clarification on any of these items. We would be glad to arrange a call and discuss everything thoroughly so that we are fully aligned.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for your patience while we prepare the contract. To keep our internal process organized, we will wait until the contract is finalized before providing an editable or downloadable version of the document. After the terms have been agreed upon, we’ll send you the PDF so you can begin working in advance.

We would like to restate the work scope we intend to put into the contract:

**1. Addition of chapters (5, as discussed earlier)**

A. Basic chapters (these are not question & answers and should be 2.5k - 3.5k words or less)

--Pre-interview preparation checklist. Since the readers already have experience, this should take a leadership-specific approach rather than covering only fundamentals. We would like to include preparation advice that is particularly relevant to leadership-level interviews.

--How to use AI for interview preparation (prompts, techniques, tools)

B. Question & Answers chapters (The author may include as many questions as they consider appropriate in each chapter, provided they account for the book’s total word count.)

--Questions candidates can ask the interviewer

--Questions intended specifically for first-time leaders

--Remote & Hybrid Leadership questions

**2. Reviewing the existing content and updating it (As agreed during the previous discussions, you will review and revise the content according to the provided directions.)**

--Refining the question set in every chapter (category) contained in the current edition, or across the 250 questions. To produce the strongest possible content, the author may recommend any of the following options:

1. Eliminate a category or combine two categories (chapters).

2. Delete individual questions after explaining the rationale.

3. Introduce new questions within a category so the new edition reflects questions being asked in today’s workplace.

4. Create a new question category if it is not already represented.

5. Recommend improved wording for any questions the author believes could be rephrased and used more effectively.

--Writing answers and supplying answers for newly added questions (as agreed: 2 mandatory and 2 subjective)

1. Mandatory answer layers: How to frame the answers, with answer frameworks incorporated here, and a sample answer.

2. Subjective answer layers: Interviewer’s intent & common mistakes

Any proposed addition or removal of a category/chapter or question must be properly reviewed by the editorial team before it can be implemented. As previously agreed, the author will examine the complete book—all 250 questions—and provide feedback to the team during the first milestone.

**3. Hybrid resources**

--Because readers do not all prefer to finish books cover-to-cover, we aim to provide a hybrid learning experience with every title. In addition to the book, we want to supply online companion resources such as checklists, AI prompts, body-language videos, mock interviews, answer templates, leadership resume tips, and any other materials you recommend.

The completed book should have an overall word count of 50k. The author must therefore plan the material around that limit and remain within it.

The author may propose other revisions or additions that could make the book more interactive and relevant for today’s readers. Those ideas will only be implemented after consultation with the editorial team.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Please confirm that these project requirements are clear and that you are comfortable proceeding.

Our team is completing the contract and will provide it to you shortly for review.

Thank you for waiting! We are eager to collaborate with you and begin this project as soon as we can.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you for examining the agreement so carefully and bringing these matters to our attention.

For the word count, 13,000 words is the accurate figure. The draft’s reference to 14,000 words was a mistake, and the final agreement will be revised accordingly.

The correct intended delivery date is **August 20, 2026**, and it should appear consistently in both locations. This date is tentative, however. After the Upwork contract officially begins, we will reassess the schedule and change the date if necessary. At present, we are aiming to finish the project in approximately one month.

On authorship credit, our decision is generally guided by three factors: applicable industry experience, particularly in leadership/senior hiring because that is the book’s subject; a degree of reputation or recognition in the field; and the quality of the writing across the complete project rather than only the initial sample.

Because the process is still at an early stage, we do not want to make that determination based only on a CV. We would prefer to continue collaborating through the next couple of chapters and evaluate the actual work. That will give everyone, including you, a much more reliable basis for deciding than a brief resume snapshot. We will revisit the subject with you directly when the project is further along.

Thank you as well for identifying the issue with the signature clause. It is supposed to require a signature on each and every page of the agreement, not the manuscript. We’ll amend that language in the final document.

I’m pleased that all other parts of the agreement are consistent with what we discussed. If you have further questions, please let us know and we will gladly provide clarification.

Best regards,
[CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

We appreciate the time you have spent on Milestones 1 and 2. Following a detailed review, our editorial team found several issues that we need to address with you directly.

**Instructional text left in the submission:** At the beginning of Milestone 1, there is a note containing direct usage directions ("delete or edit the question in suggesting mode... then paste the comment as your rationale"). This appears to be scaffolding from an AI workflow that was mistakenly not removed.

**Mention of content that does not exist:** Both the document and the manuscript text reference a "book-wide note on the first page," but no such note appears anywhere in the document.

**Submission speed:** Milestone 2, consisting of five full chapters, was delivered in roughly one day. That turnaround does not align with the level of original, in-depth analysis required for this work.

**AI-detection findings:** Independent detection tools flagged the Milestone 2 material within the 75–90% range.

Under your contract, AI-assisted tools may be used on a limited basis for spelling, grammar, research, outlining, translation, and editorial support, as long as the final manuscript represents your own original work and professional judgment. In light of the points above, the material submitted does not appear to satisfy that requirement.

Considering all of these factors, we have decided not to continue with the project. Thank you for your interest in the role and for the effort you contributed, and we wish you all the best moving forward.

Thank you.
